mainTopic: Slaughtering for nature or angels (פסולה versus זבחי מתים), and whether cutting one סימן before an idol forbids another person's animal
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה: if two people slaughter together and one of them has an improper intent, the שחיטה is invalid. The גמרא then reads the משנה closely. Because it calls slaughter for mountains and similar things only 'invalid', the animal seems not to be זבחי מתים (an idolatrous offering, forbidden even for benefit). A ברייתא seems to say the opposite. אביי answers that slaughtering for the mountain itself is only invalid, while slaughtering for the angel of the mountain makes it זבחי מתים. The ברייתא's own wording supports him, since it lists mountains together with מיכאל the angel. Next, רב הונא rules that cutting even one סימן of another person's animal before an idol forbids it. He follows רבי יוחנן's rule that bowing to someone else's animal does not forbid it, but doing an act on it does. רב נחמן then challenges רב הונא from a ברייתא that makes a person bring three חטאות for slaughtering a קרבן on שבת, outside the Temple, for an idol. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two people slaughtering together with different intentions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if two people hold one knife and slaughter, one for an improper purpose and one for a proper one, the שחיטה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two people hold a knife and slaughter together, one for the sake of one of the things listed earlier and one for a proper purpose, the slaughter is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. It says that one person's bad intention spoils a שחיטה even when a second person has a good intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה listed things like mountains, hills, rivers and deserts, and said that slaughtering for them makes the שחיטה invalid. Here it adds that the good intention of a partner does not save the animal. The improper intent of one of the two is enough to make it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The base text that the גמרא discusses
Holding a knife (here, two people holding it together)
A proper, acceptable purpose
His slaughter is invalid

phrases.english: Two people holding a knife and slaughtering,
one for the sake of one of all these,
phrases.notes: 'All these' means the list earlier in the משנה: mountains, hills, seas, rivers, deserts and similar things.

phrases.english: and one for the sake of a proper thing:
his slaughter is invalid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two people slaughter together and one has an improper intent from the משנה's list, the שחיטה is invalid.

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: invalid, but not an idolatrous offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה's wording 'invalid' that slaughtering for mountains does not make the animal זבחי מתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is invalid, yes. But it is not an offering to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and reads the משנה carefully. Because the משנה only says 'invalid', the גמרא concludes the animal is not זבחי מתים. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible outcomes. 'Invalid' means the animal is like a נבילה: you cannot eat it, but you may benefit from it. זבחי מתים is an idolatrous offering, which is forbidden even for benefit. The משנה chose the softer word, so the גמרא reads it as the softer outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
'Offerings to the dead': offerings to idols, which are forbidden even for benefit
Yes / no: a common way the גמרא spells out an inference

steps.confusionAlert: 'Invalid' (פסולה) and 'forbidden' are not the same here. פסולה means you cannot eat it, but you may still benefit from it. זבחי מתים means even benefit is forbidden.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Invalid, yes;
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier part of the משנה about slaughtering for mountains, rivers and the like.

phrases.english: offerings to the dead, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the wording of the משנה and draws a conclusion from it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Based on the משנה, slaughtering for mountains and similar things is only invalid. It is not זבחי מתים.

steps.title: A ברייתא says these are offerings to the dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists slaughtering for mountains, hills, rivers, heavenly bodies, מיכאל, and even a small worm, and calls all of these זבחי מתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction: one who slaughters for mountains, hills, rivers, deserts, the sun and moon, stars and constellations, מיכאל the great angel, or even a small worm, these are offerings to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with what it just inferred from the משנה. The ברייתא calls slaughter for mountains זבחי מתים, which is the stricter outcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (as just read) says slaughter for a mountain is only invalid. The ברייתא lists the very same kinds of things, mountains, hills, rivers and deserts, and says they are זבחי מתים, which is forbidden even for benefit. The same case seems to get two different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself
Stars and constellations
מיכאל, the great angelic prince
A small worm

phrases.english: And there is a contradiction: One who slaughters for the sake of mountains,
for the sake of hills, for the sake of rivers,
for the sake of deserts,
for the sake of the sun and moon,
for the sake of stars and constellations,
for the sake of מיכאל the great prince,
for the sake of a small worm:
these are offerings to the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that slaughtering for mountains is only invalid and not זבחי מתים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the same kind of slaughter זבחי מתים, which contradicts the משנה.

steps.title: אביי: the mountain itself versus the angel of the mountain
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the משנה is about slaughtering for the mountain itself, and the ברייתא is about slaughtering for the angel of the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There is no difficulty. This one is where he said 'for the mountain.' That one is where he said 'for the angel of the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the two sources are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering for the physical mountain is improper, so the שחיטה is invalid, but it is not idol worship. Slaughtering for the spiritual power or angel of the mountain is treated as worship, so the animal becomes זבחי מתים. The difference depends on what the person actually said he was slaughtering for.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: this introduces an answer
This one ... that one: two sources, two different cases
The angel or spiritual power of the mountain

phrases.english: אביי said: It is not difficult.
This one is where he said 'to the mountain,'
phrases.notes: 'This one' is our משנה, where the slaughter is only invalid.

phrases.english: that one is where he said 'to the angel of the mountain.'
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the ברייתא, which calls it זבחי מתים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction by splitting the cases
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same case, slaughter for a mountain
steps.terutzMaskana: Slaughter for the mountain itself is only invalid. Slaughter for the mountain's angel is זבחי מתים.

steps.title: The ברייתא's own wording supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא lists mountains right next to מיכאל the angel, which suggests it is talking about spiritual powers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it is taught together with מיכאל the great prince. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for אביי's answer from the wording of the ברייתא itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא puts the mountains in the same list as מיכאל the angel, it makes sense that the whole list is about spiritual beings. So 'mountains' in the ברייתא really means the angel of the mountain, just as אביי said. The step ends with שמע מינה: the point is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording also shows this: support from the exact words of a source
Similar to, in the same category as
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: Slaughtering for a natural thing itself (a mountain) makes the שחיטה invalid but still allowed for benefit. Slaughtering for its angel or spiritual power makes it זבחי מתים, forbidden even for benefit.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
since it is taught similar to
מיכאל the great prince.
Learn from it.

steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the ברייתא is about the angel of the mountain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא lists mountains together with מיכאל the angel

steps.title: רב הונא: cutting one סימן of another person's animal before an idol
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if someone else's animal is lying before an idol and a person cuts one סימן, he has made it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: If another person's animal was lying down before an idol, once he cut one סימן in it, he made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling of רב הונא about making an animal forbidden through idol worship, even when the animal belongs to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is not the worshipper's own. Even so, cutting just one of the two סימנים in front of the idol is enough to make it forbidden. The next step explains what this ruling is based on.

keyTerms.meaning: Another person's animal
Lying down
An idol, idol worship
One of the two organs cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe
He made it forbidden

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
If the animal of another person was
lying down before an idol,
once he cut one סימן in it,
he made it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָיְתָה בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: forbidding another person's animal through idol worship
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting one סימן of another person's animal before an idol makes it forbidden.

steps.title: The source for רב הונא: bowing does not forbid, but an action does
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב הונא follows רבי יוחנן: bowing to another person's animal does not forbid it, but doing an act on it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like what עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even though they said that one who bows to another person's animal does not make it forbidden, if he did an action with it, he made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows which earlier rule רב הונא's ruling is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן separates two cases. Bowing to someone else's animal does not forbid it. Doing a physical act on it does. Cutting one סימן is an act, so רב הונא rules that the animal becomes forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like this: shows which earlier view a ruling follows
One who bows down (in worship)
He did a physical act with it

steps.whatToRemember: Bowing to another person's animal does not forbid it. A real act on it, like cutting even one סימן before an idol, does forbid it.

phrases.english: He holds like this,
which עולא said that רבי יוחנן said:
Even though they said
one who bows to the animal of another person
did not make it forbidden,
if he did an action with it, he made it forbidden.
phrases.notes: In רב הונא's case, the 'action' is cutting one סימן.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רב הונא's ruling in an earlier principle
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that cutting one סימן forbids another person's animal
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's rule, as reported by עולא: an action on another person's animal forbids it, even though bowing does not

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא from the case of three sin offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes a ברייתא: one who slaughters a חטאת on שבת, outside the Temple, for עבודה זרה, brings three חטאות. If one סימן already forbids the animal, as רב הונא said, there should be no liability for שחוטי חוץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected to רב הונא: A ברייתא says that if someone slaughters a חטאת on שבת, outside the Temple, for an idol, he must bring three חטאות. But if you say that once he cuts one סימן for the idol the animal becomes forbidden, then he should not be liable for slaughtering outside the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks רב הונא's ruling from Step 6 by quoting a ברייתא that seems to clash with it. He starts to spell out the problem, and the full reasoning continues right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts three separate sins in one act of slaughter: working on שבת, שחוטי חוץ, and serving עבודה זרה. רב נחמן's point: if the first סימן already makes the animal forbidden as an idol offering, then by the time the slaughter is finished it is no longer a proper קרבן. So how can the slaughter still count as שחוטי חוץ?

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering, brought for doing certain sins by accident
The sin of slaughtering a קרבן outside the Temple courtyard
Three sin offerings, one for each separate sin done in a single act
He made it forbidden
And if you say, which introduces the opinion being attacked

steps.confusionAlert: The animal here is a חטאת set aside as a קרבן. Even when its owner slaughters it, רש״י explains, it counts as not his, because it belongs to Heaven. So, just like in רב הונא's case, he is acting on an animal that isn't his own. The ברייתא is not about bringing a חטאת as a קרבן. It is about slaughtering one in the wrong place, at the wrong time, for the wrong purpose. The 'three חטאות' are what he must bring afterward to atone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tests whether רב הונא's rule, that one סימן is enough to forbid the animal, can fit with a ברייתא that treats the whole slaughter as one complete act of שחוטי חוץ.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman raised an objection to Rav Huna:
One who slaughters a sin offering on Shabbat
outside the Temple, for idol worship,
is liable to bring three sin offerings.
phrases.notes: One for working on שבת, one for slaughtering a קרבן outside, and one for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: And if you say,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁחַט בָּהּ סִימָן אֶחָד אֲסָרָהּ –
phrases.english: once he cut one siman in it, he made it forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is רב הונא's ruling from Step 6.

phrases.english: then he should not be liable for slaughtering outside the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling (Step 6), which Step 7 had tied to רבי יוחנן, using a ברייתא about three חטאות.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that cutting one סימן for an idol forbids the animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the slaughterer liable for שחוטי חוץ, which assumes the whole slaughter was done on a proper קרבן. If the first סימן already forbids the animal, the slaughter would finish on a forbidden animal, so there should be no liability for שחוטי חוץ.
